# Evidence matrix

Test set v0.1.0 · type set v0.1.0 · scoring v0.1.0

Evidence level sets the item weight: **established** = 1, **emerging** = 0.5, **exploratory** = 0.

## ATT: Attention Drift

Difficulty sustaining voluntary attention and resisting distraction in everyday tasks, conversations and media.

Dimension sources: [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Kessler et al., 2005](references.md#kessler2005); [Seli et al., 2015](references.md#seli2015); [Sedgwick et al., 2019](references.md#sedgwick2019)

| ID | Statement | Keyed | Level | Weight | Basis | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| ATT-01 | My mind wanders off during conversations, even when I want to listen. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR ADHD A1(c): seems not to listen when spoken to; mind-wandering linked to ADHD symptoms | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Seli et al., 2015](references.md#seli2015); [Kessler et al., 2005](references.md#kessler2005) |
| ATT-02 | I make careless mistakes because I miss small details in instructions. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR ADHD A1(a): careless mistakes, overlooks details | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Kessler et al., 2005](references.md#kessler2005) |
| ATT-03 | I lose the thread of a film or show because my thoughts drift elsewhere. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR ADHD A1(b): difficulty sustaining attention, including in leisure activities | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Seli et al., 2015](references.md#seli2015) |
| ATT-04 | Movements or conversations nearby easily pull my focus away from a task. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR ADHD A1(h): easily distracted by extraneous stimuli | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Kessler et al., 2005](references.md#kessler2005) |
| ATT-05 | I can keep my attention on a dull task until it is finished. | reverse | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR ADHD A1(b)/(f): sustaining effort on tasks that need sustained mental effort | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Kessler et al., 2005](references.md#kessler2005) |
| ATT-06 | I find it easy to stay focused during long meetings or lectures. | reverse | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR ADHD A1(b): sustaining attention during lectures, conversations or lengthy reading | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Kessler et al., 2005](references.md#kessler2005) |

## IMP: Restless Energy

Motor and inner restlessness, plus impulsive responding (speaking, deciding or acting before considering consequences).

Dimension sources: [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Kessler et al., 2005](references.md#kessler2005); [Barkley, 1997](references.md#barkley1997); [Sedgwick et al., 2019](references.md#sedgwick2019)

| ID | Statement | Keyed | Level | Weight | Basis | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| IMP-01 | I feel restless inside when I have to sit still for a long time. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR ADHD A2(c): in adults may be limited to feeling restless | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Kessler et al., 2005](references.md#kessler2005) |
| IMP-02 | I answer questions before the other person has finished asking them. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR ADHD A2(g): blurts out an answer before a question has been completed | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Kessler et al., 2005](references.md#kessler2005) |
| IMP-03 | I buy things on impulse and regret it later. | forward | emerging | 0.5 | Impulsive decision-making follows from the behavioural-inhibition model of ADHD; not a DSM criterion, so weighted as emerging | [Barkley, 1997](references.md#barkley1997) |
| IMP-04 | I fidget with my hands or feet when I am supposed to be still. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR ADHD A2(a): fidgets with or taps hands or feet | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Kessler et al., 2005](references.md#kessler2005) |
| IMP-05 | I find it easy to wait my turn, for example in a queue. | reverse | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR ADHD A2(h): difficulty waiting their turn | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Kessler et al., 2005](references.md#kessler2005) |
| IMP-06 | I usually think through the consequences before I act. | reverse | established | 1 | Behavioural inhibition as the core of ADHD impulsivity (DSM-5-TR A2; Barkley 1997) | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Barkley, 1997](references.md#barkley1997) |
| PRF-06 | I concentrate better when I can move around, for example pacing or walking while I think. | forward | emerging | 0.5 | In ADHD, more movement during cognitive tasks is associated with better working-memory performance | [Sarver et al., 2015](references.md#sarver2015) |

## EXF: Executive Load

Day-to-day executive functioning: time estimation, task initiation, organisation, planning and prospective memory.

Dimension sources: [Barkley, 1997](references.md#barkley1997); [Barkley, 2011](references.md#barkley2011); [Hill, 2004](references.md#hill2004); [Kirby et al., 2010](references.md#kirby2010)

| ID | Statement | Keyed | Level | Weight | Basis | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| EXF-01 | I underestimate how long tasks will take and end up running late. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR ADHD A1(e) lists poor time management; timing differences shown in neurocognitive studies | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Noreika et al., 2013](references.md#noreika2013); [Barkley, 1997](references.md#barkley1997) |
| EXF-02 | I put off starting important tasks, even when I want to start early. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR ADHD A1(f): avoids or delays tasks needing sustained effort; procrastination linked to inattention | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Niermann & Scheres, 2014](references.md#niermann2014) |
| EXF-03 | I misplace everyday items such as my keys, phone or wallet. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR ADHD A1(g): loses things such as keys, wallet or phone | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Kessler et al., 2005](references.md#kessler2005) |
| EXF-04 | Breaking a big project into smaller steps feels overwhelming to me. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR ADHD A1(e): difficulty organising tasks; BDEFS self-organisation facet | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Barkley, 2011](references.md#barkley2011) |
| EXF-05 | I keep my belongings and paperwork well organised without much effort. | reverse | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR ADHD A1(e): keeping materials and belongings in order | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Barkley, 2011](references.md#barkley2011) |
| EXF-06 | I remember appointments and deadlines without needing reminders. | reverse | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR ADHD A1(i): forgetful in daily activities, e.g. keeping appointments | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Barkley, 2011](references.md#barkley2011) |

## SOC: Social Decoding

Effort needed to read implicit social communication (tone, sarcasm, facial expression, unwritten rules), including scripting and directness.

Dimension sources: [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Baron-Cohen et al., 2001](references.md#baroncohen2001); [Milton, 2012](references.md#milton2012); [Hull et al., 2019](references.md#hull2019); [Russell et al., 2019](references.md#russell2019)

| ID | Statement | Keyed | Level | Weight | Basis | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| SOC-01 | I find it hard to tell when someone is joking or being sarcastic. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR autism A1/A2; difficulty with non-literal language such as sarcasm (Strange Stories) | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Happé, 1994](references.md#happe1994); [Baron-Cohen et al., 2001](references.md#baroncohen2001) |
| SOC-02 | Small talk feels like hard work, even with friendly people. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR autism A1: differences in back-and-forth conversation; AQ social skill subscale | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Baron-Cohen et al., 2001](references.md#baroncohen2001) |
| SOC-03 | People have told me I seem blunt when I was simply being honest. | forward | emerging | 0.5 | DSM-5-TR autism A3 (adjusting behaviour to social context); directness and honesty reported as autistic traits | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Russell et al., 2019](references.md#russell2019); [Milton, 2012](references.md#milton2012) |
| SOC-04 | I plan or rehearse what to say before ordinary social situations. | forward | emerging | 0.5 | Scripting and rehearsal are camouflaging strategies measured by the CAT-Q | [Hull et al., 2019](references.md#hull2019); [Lai et al., 2017](references.md#lai2017) |
| SOC-05 | I can usually tell how someone feels from their face or tone of voice. | reverse | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR autism A2 (non-verbal communication); meta-analytic evidence for emotion-recognition differences | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Uljarevic & Hamilton, 2013](references.md#uljarevic2013) |
| SOC-06 | I quickly pick up the unwritten rules when I join a new group. | reverse | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR autism A3: understanding relationships and implicit social rules | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Baron-Cohen et al., 2001](references.md#baroncohen2001) |

## SEN: Sensory Intensity

Heightened responsiveness to sensory input (auditory, visual, tactile, olfactory) and susceptibility to sensory overload.

Dimension sources: [Dunn, 1997](references.md#dunn1997); [Ben-Sasson et al., 2009](references.md#bensasson2009); [Bijlenga et al., 2017](references.md#bijlenga2017); [Panagiotidi et al., 2018](references.md#panagiotidi2018); [Robertson & Simmons, 2013](references.md#robertson2013)

|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|

| SEN-02 | Clothing labels, seams or certain fabrics bother me so much that I avoid them. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR autism B4: adverse response to specific textures; heightened tactile sensitivity | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Cascio et al., 2008](references.md#cascio2008); [Tavassoli et al., 2014](references.md#tavassoli2014) |
| SEN-03 | Bright or flickering lights quickly wear me out. | forward | established | 1 | Visual hypersensitivity in autism and self-reported photophobia in adult ADHD | [Simmons et al., 2009](references.md#simmons2009); [Kooij & Bijlenga, 2014](references.md#kooij2014); [Robertson & Simmons, 2013](references.md#robertson2013) |
| SEN-04 | In busy places like supermarkets, all the noise, light and movement overwhelms me. | forward | established | 1 | Sensory over-responsivity elevated in autism (meta-analysis) and adult ADHD; AASP sensation avoiding | [Ben-Sasson et al., 2009](references.md#bensasson2009); [Bijlenga et al., 2017](references.md#bijlenga2017); [Brown, 2002](references.md#brown2002) |

Preference for sameness and predictability, discomfort with unexpected change, and intense, focused interests or detail-oriented perception.

Dimension sources: [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Baron-Cohen et al., 2001](references.md#baroncohen2001); [Russell et al., 2019](references.md#russell2019)

|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|

| RTN-02 | I have intense interests that I could think or talk about for hours. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR autism B3: restricted interests that are abnormal in intensity or focus | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Russell et al., 2019](references.md#russell2019) |
| RTN-03 | I notice small details or patterns that other people tend to miss. | forward | emerging | 0.5 | AQ attention-to-detail subscale; less specific to autism than other subscales | [Baron-Cohen et al., 2001](references.md#baroncohen2001) |
| RTN-04 | I prefer to do everyday things in exactly the same way each time. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR autism B2: inflexible adherence to routines | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022) |
| RTN-05 | I enjoy spontaneous changes of plan. | reverse | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR autism B2: insistence on sameness, difficulty with transitions | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022) |
| RTN-06 | I like trying a new route, restaurant or method just for variety. | reverse | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR autism B2: need to take the same route or eat the same food every day | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022) |

## LIT: Word Decoding

Phonological and orthographic processing in everyday reading and spelling: speed, accuracy, letter/word confusions and decoding new words.

Dimension sources: [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Vellutino et al., 2004](references.md#vellutino2004); [Peterson & Pennington, 2012](references.md#peterson2012); [Lefly & Pennington, 2000](references.md#lefly2000); [Taylor & Vestergaard, 2022](references.md#taylor2022)

| ID | Statement | Keyed | Level | Weight | Basis | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| LIT-01 | Reading takes me noticeably longer than it takes most people. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR specific learning disorder A1: slow, effortful word reading; persists in adults | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Peterson & Pennington, 2012](references.md#peterson2012); [Lefly & Pennington, 2000](references.md#lefly2000) |
| LIT-02 | Spelling is hard for me, even with words I use often. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR specific learning disorder A3: difficulties with spelling | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Peterson & Pennington, 2012](references.md#peterson2012); [Lefly & Pennington, 2000](references.md#lefly2000) |
| LIT-03 | I mix up similar-looking letters or words, like b/d or "was"/"saw". | forward | emerging | 0.5 | Letter and word confusions are commonly reported, but reversal errors are not specific to dyslexia, so weighted as emerging | [Vellutino et al., 2004](references.md#vellutino2004) |
| LIT-04 | I stumble over words when I read aloud. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR specific learning disorder A1: inaccurate word reading (oral reading) | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Lefly & Pennington, 2000](references.md#lefly2000) |
| LIT-05 | I can easily sound out long, unfamiliar words. | reverse | established | 1 | Phonological decoding of unfamiliar words is the core deficit in dyslexia | [Vellutino et al., 2004](references.md#vellutino2004); [Peterson & Pennington, 2012](references.md#peterson2012) |
| LIT-06 | I can quickly skim a page and pick out the key words. | reverse | emerging | 0.5 | Reading efficiency; skimming draws on fluency but also on strategy, so weighted as emerging | [Peterson & Pennington, 2012](references.md#peterson2012) |

## NUM: Number Sense

Everyday numerical processing: mental arithmetic, magnitude comparison, quantity estimation, digit sequencing and number-fact retrieval.

Dimension sources: [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Butterworth, 2005](references.md#butterworth2005); [Butterworth et al., 2011](references.md#butterworth2011)

| ID | Statement | Keyed | Level | Weight | Basis | Sources |
|---|---|---|---|---:|---|---|
| NUM-01 | Mental arithmetic, such as working out change, is slow or stressful for me. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR specific learning disorder A5: number facts and calculation | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Butterworth et al., 2011](references.md#butterworth2011) |
| NUM-02 | I find it hard to judge how many things are in a small group at a glance. | forward | emerging | 0.5 | Slower subitising and impaired number acuity in dyscalculia (lab evidence; self-report not yet validated) | [Schleifer & Landerl, 2011](references.md#schleifer2011); [Piazza et al., 2010](references.md#piazza2010) |
| NUM-03 | I swap or reverse digits when copying numbers like phone numbers or codes. | forward | exploratory | 0 | Digit transposition is often reported by adults with dyscalculia, but no peer-reviewed evidence was found. Collected for pilot analysis and not scored | _none_ |
| NUM-04 | Reading analogue clocks or timetables is harder for me than for most people. | forward | emerging | 0.5 | Applied numeracy (time, schedules) depends on number sense; DSM-5-TR A5/A6 | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Butterworth, 2005](references.md#butterworth2005) |
| NUM-05 | I can easily compare two prices to see which is the better deal. | reverse | established | 1 | Magnitude comparison is a core marker of dyscalculia | [Piazza et al., 2010](references.md#piazza2010); [Butterworth et al., 2011](references.md#butterworth2011) |
| NUM-06 | I remember number facts, such as times tables, without effort. | reverse | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR specific learning disorder A5: difficulty mastering number facts | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Butterworth et al., 2011](references.md#butterworth2011) |

Dimension sources: [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Blank et al., 2019](references.md#blank2019); [Kirby et al., 2010](references.md#kirby2010)

| ID | Statement | Keyed | Level | Weight | Basis | Sources |

| MOT-02 | Handwriting is tiring for me, or others find it hard to read. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR DCD A: slow or inaccurate handwriting | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Kirby et al., 2010](references.md#kirby2010); [Blank et al., 2019](references.md#blank2019) |

| MOT-04 | Fiddly tasks like tying laces, doing up buttons or using scissors are awkward for me. | forward | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR DCD A: fine motor tasks such as using scissors or cutlery | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Kirby et al., 2010](references.md#kirby2010) |
| MOT-05 | I would describe myself as physically well coordinated. | reverse | established | 1 | Global coordination self-rating (ADC checklist) | [Kirby et al., 2010](references.md#kirby2010); [Blank et al., 2019](references.md#blank2019) |
| MOT-06 | I can catch a ball thrown to me without much difficulty. | reverse | established | 1 | DSM-5-TR DCD A: catching an object | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Kirby et al., 2010](references.md#kirby2010) |

## Types

| Type | Associated with | Sources |
|---|---|---|
| The Spark | Traits often associated with ADHD (combined presentation) | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Kessler et al., 2005](references.md#kessler2005); [Sedgwick et al., 2019](references.md#sedgwick2019); [Ashinoff & Abu-Akel, 2021](references.md#ashinoff2021) |
| The Daydreamer | Traits often associated with ADHD (predominantly inattentive presentation) | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Kessler et al., 2005](references.md#kessler2005); [Seli et al., 2015](references.md#seli2015) |
| The Deep Diver | Traits often associated with autism | [American Psychiatric Association, 2022](references.md#apa2022); [Baron-Cohen et al., 2001](references.md#baroncohen2001); [Ben-Sasson et al., 2009](references.md#bensasson2009); [Hill, 2004](references.md#hill2004); [Russell et al., 2019](references.md#russell2019) |
| The Kaleidoscope | Traits often associated with co-occurring autism and ADHD (sometimes called AuDHD) | [Rong et al., 2021](references.md#rong2021); [Bijlenga et al., 2017](references.md#bijlenga2017); [Hull et al., 2019](references.md#hull2019) |
| The Storyteller | Traits often associated with dyslexia | [Peterson & Pennington, 2012](references.md#peterson2012); [Landerl & Moll, 2010](references.md#landerl2010); [Taylor & Vestergaard, 2022](references.md#taylor2022) |
| The Wordsmith | Traits often associated with dyscalculia | [Butterworth et al., 2011](references.md#butterworth2011); [Landerl & Moll, 2010](references.md#landerl2010) |
| The Improviser | Traits often associated with dyspraxia (developmental coordination disorder) | [Blank et al., 2019](references.md#blank2019); [Kirby et al., 2010](references.md#kirby2010) |
| The Tuner | Traits often associated with sensory processing sensitivity | [Aron & Aron, 1997](references.md#aron1997); [Dunn, 1997](references.md#dunn1997); [Panagiotidi et al., 2018](references.md#panagiotidi2018) |
| The Navigator | No elevated neurodivergent trait pattern on the measured dimensions | [Lai et al., 2017](references.md#lai2017); [Haslam et al., 2020](references.md#haslam2020) |
| The Mosaic | Elevated traits in a combination that doesn't match one prototype closely | [Haslam et al., 2020](references.md#haslam2020) |
